html:
Gustavia is the harbour town of Saint Barthelemy, renamed in 1785 after King Gustav III of Sweden, who had just gained the island. It was a free port, open to ships of all nations.

In the wars of the late 1700s the port handled goods, and enslaved people, passing between the warring empires.

After the island returned to France in 1878 the town shrank. From the late 20th century it became a resort for the very rich, with yachts filling the harbour. Old Swedish buildings and street names still recall Swedish rule, and flights arrive mostly via Princess Juliana Airport.
